reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: With a realistic life-mean aged SR of ~0.86 (porous inorganic surfaces in dusty hot climates lose 0.05-0.10) against a life-mean ~0.70 for the repainted acrylic, the same sol-air model gives ~30 % less roof heat flux; facades see less sun and half the sky, so over roof plus facades (windows excluded) the contribution is ~20 %.
key_assumption_issues: Service-life aged reflectance loss of 0.06 is an assumption; open porosity (60 % voids) traps fine dust and there is no field data for 20 years
Dry-climate net sky longwave (85 W/m2); in humid hot climates 40-60 W/m2 shrinks the emittance advantage
Daily-mean linearised model; baseline repainted every 10 years has a life-mean SR nearer 0.70 than 0.67
Only the roof is modelled while the objective covers roof and facades
killer_risks: Dust and biofilm pick-up in the open porous surface erodes most of the advantage within a few years
Potassium silicate on roofs: brittle, cracks on moving substrates and fails under ponding water
Glare to neighbours from very white surfaces

reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: A sealed 40 mm cavity with a clean low-e face gives ~0.5 m2K/W, but tile joints leak and the low-e face collects dust, so ~0.3 m2K/W is realistic, i.e. ~18 % less facade flux; since the same resistance is available from 1-2 cm of conventional insulation and only facades are treated, its contribution to the envelope objective is ~8 %.
key_assumption_issues: Gain mostly from the assumed cavity resistance (0.5 m2K/W), which is conventional insulation, not from the bionic reflective shell (~5 %)
Assumes a sealed cavity; real ceramic rainscreens are open-jointed
Low-e face stays clean for 20 years
killer_risks: Cost and weight (100-180 EUR/m2, 20-25 kg/m2) versus paint plus 2 cm insulation
Condensation and dust in the sealed chambers degrade the low-e face

reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: Chalking surfaces do stay whiter than acrylics, but dirt also sticks to rough chalky surfaces and erosion in arid climates is slow; I expect the soiling-driven SR loss reduced by about a third (aged ~0.78 vs 0.70 life-mean), i.e. ~15 % less roof heat flux and ~12 % over the envelope.
reviews.proxy_reason: Gain equals the assumed erosion-rate ratio (v_b+k_w)/(v_d+k_w) with k_abs calibrated to the baseline loss; nothing independent is solved.
key_assumption_issues: Erosion rate of 20 um/yr assumed and not physically derived; it controls the whole result
Same wash-off and dirt absorption coefficient for smooth acrylic and a rough chalky surface
Freshly exposed subsurface assumed as white as the clean surface; UV-damaged and microcracked layers are not
killer_risks: Erosion is climate-dependent: no renewal in arid climates, erosion-through in wet ones
Chalk runoff stains facades below, rubs off, clogs gutters
Weak cohesion: hail, foot traffic and wind scouring damage the roof unevenly
